jamal (oncall): Heads up - we're seeing a gap in paging. Incident bot posted to #incidents but PagerDuty didn't create an incident or page the on-call. Customer-visible: several tenants hit 502s around 09:12 UTC.

incident-bot: [automated] alert received: service: inference-gateway severity: critical. attempted routing: primary -> pagerduty. result: suppressed (rule match).

carla (support): I'm seeing a spike in support tickets and a few customers reported degraded responses. putting links to a couple of tickets: https://zendesk.example/ticket/12345, https://zendesk.example/ticket/12346

sara (sre): Thanks. jamal, can you paste the alert payload and the suppressor decision log?

jamal (oncall): paste: ```{\n  "alert": "inference-gateway-502-rate",\n  "severity": "critical",\n  "tags": ["route:ops-prod", "team:runtime"]\n}``` suppressor log: ```decision=SUPPRESS rule_id=cfg/alert-suppressor re_match=^route:ops$ matched_field=tags reason="matched exact tag"\nhttp_response=200 to pagerduty gateway```

michael (infra): quick check: our pager webhook returned 200, but the body shows `ack_required=false` which is odd. curl output: ```{"status":"ok","ack_required":false}```. That implies our gateway flagged it as non-pageable.

carla (support): is that why PD didn't page? We definitely had critical errors. Customers impacted.

jamal (oncall): I just tried re-sending the same alert with modified tags (route:ops) and it got through and paged. Looks like the suppressor is too strict and doesn't account for the new suffix `-prod`.

incident-bot: [automated] re-run of alert id 8491: routed to pagerduty -> created incident PD-7891.

sara (sre): OK that's a reproducible trigger. The suppressor config uses an anchored regex `^route:ops$` which won't match `route:ops-prod`. But logs show the suppressor matched — maybe reverse logic: the code is using `match != true` or a negation. michael, can you grep the suppressor code?

michael (infra): found it. In notify/suppressor.go we accidentally flipped the return in `ShouldSuppress()` after a refactor. snippet: ```if re.MatchString(tag) { return false } // previously returned true by mistake``` so it does the opposite now for some paths. There's also a second check that iterates tags and applies the inverse. oops.

jamal (oncall): Fix idea: quick patch to revert logic and rotate the config to a temporary allowlist. I'll deploy a small hotfix to staging then prod.

deploy-bot: [ci] build #4821 passed -> deploying notify-service:hotfix/suppressor-logic to prod in 2m.

michael (infra): Before prod deploy, recommend we disable the suppressor entirely for 10m as a mitigation so new critical alerts page. Command: `kubectl annotate svc/notify disable-suppressor=true --overwrite` (we have a small operator that respects that). jamal can do that now?

jamal (oncall): Doing it now. `kubectl annotate ...` -> annotated. testing with synthetic alert... synthetic alert routed to pagerduty and paging succeeded :thumbsup:

carla (support): confirmed PD incident created and customers paged. I'll update the support tickets and let customers know we're investigating the root cause and have restored paging.

jamal (oncall): Deploying hotfix now.

deploy-bot: [ci] notify-service:hotfix/suppressor-logic deployed to prod (revision 1.2.3-hotfix).

michael (infra): Verified code logic: `ShouldSuppress()` restored to expected semantics. Added unit test for route variants and a fallback that treats unknown tag suffixes as non-suppressible. Pushed to main.

incident-bot: [automated] previously suppressed alerts re-evaluated: 7 alerts re-routed -> 5 created as PD incidents.

sara (sre): Good containment. Next steps: 1) postmortem (assign owners), 2) audit suppressor rules for other anchored regexes, 3) add integration test exercising PD path (end-to-end).

carla (support): I'll draft the customer message and post to #customer-comm.

jamal (oncall): TL;DR: paging stopped due to inverted suppressor logic after refactor + anchored regex gaps. Mitigation: temporarily disabled suppressor + hotfix deployed. Customer impact: multiple tenants saw 502 spikes, support tickets opened; no long-lived data loss. Postmortem planned.

michael (infra): I'll open a PR for the postmortem and list the deploy/CI steps to prevent accidental logic inversion during refactors.

carla (support): Marking this as P1-> retrospective required. Please ping me if you need quotes for customer comms.

jamal (oncall): leaving a note to oncall rotation: if paging stops, try `curl -X POST https://notify.internal/retry?alert_id=<id>` as an immediate workaround and annotate suppression flag as shown above.

sara (sre): assigning incident #INC-2026-084 to jamal/michael/carol (postmortem owner = michael). setting postmortem due by EOD+3.

carla (support): thanks everyone. closing live mitigation thread, will re-open if anything reappears. :white_check_mark:
